title: Can Wasm help us run fewer servers?
subtitle: Sustainable computing · Java services vs Rust/Wasm on wasmCloud
notes: The question is useful work per physical machine while meeting a service target. This deck evaluates evidence for consolidation, not a universal runtime ranking. Measurements are from this repository on a local MacBook setup, through 8 November 2026.

title: Memory density: a strong, bounded result
subtitle: 25 orders/s per application · CPU headroom · p95 target below 100 ms
notes: Java 2 GiB passed all three; next 1 GiB suffered observed OOMs under equal service splits. This is not an optimized JVM minimum. Wasm 512 MiB passed all; 384 MiB passed two, third inconclusive for insufficient CPU telemetry, not proven saturation. At 256 MiB two OOMs. The 4-versus-16 projection divides an application-only 8 GiB pool by passing caps. It excludes shared platform overhead and concurrent interactions. Do not apply these short 25/s caps to long-lived 350/s workloads.

title: The machine profile can reverse the answer
subtitle: Illustrative packing ceilings from the 100/s resource profile, not deployment sizing.
notes: Arithmetic illustration only, using rounded footprint medians: Java 2739 MiB/.275 cores and Wasm 323 MiB/.511 cores at 100/s each. floor(min(memory/RAM, CPU/cores)). 4 GiB gives Java1/Wasm7;32 GiB givesJava11/Wasm7. Pools are already assumed net of infrastructure reservations; additional safety headroom and peaks reduce counts. No such concurrent packing trial was run. Mean working sets are not safe resource limits. Wasm growth, databases, network contention, SLA and shared runtime scaling can invalidate linear extrapolation. These numbers demonstrate bottleneck reversal, not a sales forecast.

items.text: The machine profile can reverse the answer
Illustrative packing ceilings from the 100/s resource profile, not deployment sizing.
copies ≤ min(RAM pool ÷ RAM per copy, CPU pool ÷ CPU per copy)
Wasm favors memory-tight, CPU-rich hosts; Java may fit CPU-tight hosts better.

title: Sustainability: what we can—and cannot—claim
subtitle: Resource measurements support a hypothesis; they do not measure its environmental outcome.
notes: The proposed mechanism is consolidation of a memory-bound fleet. A system using more CPU may still enable a smaller fleet, or may instead hit a CPU bottleneck. Which outcome dominates requires real hosts, workload mixes, reservations and energy measurements. No emission factors, cloud prices or energy-per-core conversion have been assumed.

items.text: Resource measurements support a hypothesis; they do not measure its environmental outcome.

Less application RAM
Faster first accepted order
More loaded CPU
Usually higher p95 latency

Fewer physical servers
Lower kWh per accepted order
Lower lifecycle carbon
Stable long-term packed density
CPU-seconds and MiB are useful indicators. Neither is a carbon measurement.

title: A practical replacement decision
subtitle: Choose by the bottleneck and service target, rather than runtime preference.
notes: These are recommendations inferred from measured trade-offs, not additional tests. Wasm reliability required a locally patched host and HTTP provider; the operational burden and maintenance of that patch must be part of adoption planning. Java allocation optimization must be retained in a fair production comparison.

items.text: Choose by the bottleneck and service target, rather than runtime preference.
A targeted pilot is supported; a blanket migration claim is not.

title: The next proof should be fewer real machines
subtitle: A production-shaped consolidation trial, rather than another isolated latency benchmark.
notes: Proposed future acceptance test, not an executed result. Include databases, brokers, operators, sidecars, storage, ingress and monitoring. Measure service completion if accepted orders are asynchronous. Use several trials and a long enough soak to resolve growth; do not aim for100%CPU if it breaks latency/headroom requirements. Measure actual host energy at equal delivered load instead of inferring it from utilization.

title: Evidence and reproducibility
subtitle: Keep the conclusion attached to the tested system and the retained raw results.
notes: Frozen runtime: wasmCloud1.9.2-regack.1 and HTTP provider0.25.0-regack.1. Subscriber registration acknowledgement patches in both host/provider transports. Execution limit5s,RPC4s. Ignored .results files must be exported separately if distributing this repository; the deck itself is self-contained.
